diagnostic_criteria: High Risk LDL-C: >= 160 mg/dL without overt ASCVD, or >= 70 mg/dL in patients with established ASCVD or Diabetes
Low HDL-C: < 40 mg/dL in males, < 50 mg/dL in females
Atherogenic Dyslipidemia: Elevated triglycerides + low HDL-C + elevated small dense LDL particles
recommended_investigations: Fasting lipid profile after a 10-12 hour overnight fast
Liver Function Tests (ALT/AST) and Serum Creatinine prior to statin therapy initiation
Serum Creatine Phosphokinase (CPK) if muscle pain or myopathy symptoms develop
Fasting Blood Glucose and HbA1c to screen for concomitant metabolic syndrome
Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH) to exclude secondary dyslipidemia due to hypothyroidism
lifestyle_precautions: Reduction of saturated fatty acid intake to < 7% of daily caloric consumption
Eliminate vanaspati, dalda, palm oil, and deep-fried bakery snacks containing industrial trans-fats
Incorporate soluble dietary fiber (oats, isabgol, flaxseed, beans) to bind enterohepatic cholesterol
Minimum 150 minutes/week of moderate aerobic exercise (brisk walk 30 mins x 5 days/week)
Attain and sustain body mass index (BMI) < 23 kg/m² and waist circumference < 90 cm (men) / < 80 cm (women)
Complete cessation of tobacco usage in all smoking and smokeless forms

medicines.name: Atorvastatin
medicines.purpose: Moderate to High-intensity HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitor
medicines.notes: 10 mg to 20 mg once daily at bedtime for primary prevention; 40 mg to 80 mg once daily for high-risk secondary prevention.

medicines.name: Rosuvastatin
medicines.purpose: High-intensity statin therapy for potent LDL reduction
medicines.notes: 5 mg to 10 mg once daily for primary ASCVD prevention; 20 mg once daily for high-risk patients. Monitor renal function in elderly.

medicines.name: Fenofibrate
medicines.notes: 145 mg to 160 mg once daily with meals. Indicated when triglycerides persist > 200 mg/dL after statin optimization. Avoid gemfibrozil with statins.

medicines.name: Ezetimibe
medicines.notes: 10 mg once daily co-administered with statins when LDL-C targets are not achieved on maximum tolerated statin dose.

red_flags_refer_to_doctor: New-onset exertional retrosternal chest tightness, squeezing, or pain radiating to left arm or jaw
Unexplained persistent muscle pain, weakness, tenderness, or brown-colored urine (suspected rhabdomyolysis)
Severe hypertriglyceridemia (> 500 mg/dL) presenting with acute abdominal pain (risk of acute pancreatitis)
Uncontrolled jaundice or persistent right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness
follow_up: Repeat fasting lipid profile 6-8 weeks following initiation or titration of lipid-lowering therapy
Annual lipid profile monitoring once therapeutic LDL-C target has been stabilized
Evaluate treatment adherence and lifestyle compliance at every clinical consultation
